stem: Describe the role of SADC in the socio-economic development of southern Africa.

points.description: Transport corridors (Beira, Maputo, Nacala).
Southern African Power Pool shares electricity.
Free Trade Area (2008) reduces tariffs.
Food security / drought early warning.
Health programmes (HIV and AIDS, malaria).
Peace, mediation and election observation support development.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: SADC develops transport corridors such as Beira and Maputo so landlocked states can reach the sea. The Power Pool lets members share electricity. The Free Trade Area of 2008 cut tariffs on trade between members. SADC runs drought early-warning and food security programmes and joint health programmes against HIV and AIDS and malaria. Its mediation and election observation help keep the peace needed for development.

hints: Think of transport, energy, trade, food, health and peace.

stem: Explain **two** failures or weaknesses of SADC.

points.description: Identifies a weakness (e.g. donor dependence / slow implementation).
Explains its effect.
Identifies a second weakness (e.g. South African dominance / overlapping memberships / divisions).
Explains its effect.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: SADC has depended heavily on foreign donors, so many projects were shaped by donors' priorities and stalled when money ran out. South Africa's economy is far larger than the others, so it gains most from free trade while smaller members struggle to compete.

stem:
Study the source and answer the questions.

**Source A** — a speech by a fictional delegate at a regional business forum in Gaborone, 2012 (invented for this question)

> Thirty years ago a truck from Lusaka to the sea had to pass through apartheid South Africa. Today we have the corridors, the Power Pool and a free trade area. Yet a trader in Bulawayo still waits days at a border post, our factories still buy more from outside the region than from each other, and many projects still wait for money from abroad.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Identify **three** achievements of regional co-operation mentioned in Source A.

points.description: Transport corridors.
The Power Pool.
A free trade area.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: What problems of SADC does the delegate identify?

points.description: Delays at border posts.
Members trade more with outsiders than with each other.
Dependence on foreign funding for projects.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: How far does Source A give a balanced view of SADC's record? Use the source and your own knowledge.

points.description: Balanced: gives both achievements and problems.
Own knowledge confirms achievements (Beira corridor, Power Pool 1995, FTA 2008).
Own knowledge confirms problems (donor dependence, low intra-regional trade).
Omits: peace and mediation work (Zimbabwe 2008, Lesotho, Madagascar).
Omits: political criticisms (Tribunal suspension, divisions over the DRC).
Supported judgement; provenance: a business forum focuses on trade.

levels.descriptor: Developed explanation of several relevant factors or arguments, supported by accurate, specific knowledge, considering more than one side and reaching a supported judgement that answers the question.
Some explanation of one or two relevant factors, or several points described with limited explanation; little or no judgement.
Simple, general or narrative statements with limited relevance to the question; little explanation.
One or two relevant but undeveloped points.

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
The source is fairly balanced, since it lists achievements, the corridors, the Power Pool and the free trade area, and also problems such as border delays, low trade between members and dependence on foreign funding. My own knowledge confirms these: the Beira corridor and the Power Pool of 1995 are real achievements, and donor dependence has long weakened SADC.

However, the delegate was speaking at a business forum, so he concentrates on trade and infrastructure. He leaves out SADC's peace work, such as mediation in Zimbabwe in 2008, and political criticisms, such as the suspension of the Tribunal in 2010 and divisions over the DRC.

So the source is balanced on economic matters but gives an incomplete view of SADC's whole record.

explanation: Source-based practice question on SADC's record (12 marks).
hints: Find both achievements and problems in the source.

points.description: Economic growth and poverty reduction.
Regional integration and free trade.
Peace, security and democracy.
Shared resources and the environment / links between peoples / fighting disease.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: To what extent did SADCC achieve its aim of reducing dependence on South Africa before it was replaced by SADC?

points.description: Achieved: corridors (Beira, Maputo, Nacala) rebuilt; Beira protected by Zimbabwean troops.
Achieved: international aid attracted; sectoral co-ordination built co-operation.
Not achieved: South African destabilisation (support for RENAMO) damaged corridors.
Not achieved: Lesotho, Swaziland, Botswana remained in a customs union with South Africa; migrant labour and trade continued.
Not achieved: donor dependence replaced one dependence with another.
Supported judgement.

levels.descriptor: Developed explanation of several relevant factors or arguments, supported by accurate, specific knowledge, considering more than one side and reaching a supported judgement that answers the question.
Some explanation of one or two relevant factors, or several points described with limited explanation; little or no judgement.
Simple, general or narrative statements with limited relevance to the question; little explanation.

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
SADCC had some success. It made transport its first priority, and the Beira, Maputo and Nacala corridors were rebuilt with international funding, giving landlocked states routes to the sea that avoided South Africa. Zimbabwean troops protected the Beira corridor. SADCC attracted a great deal of foreign aid, and the sectoral system, with each member leading one area, built habits of co-operation.

But dependence was far from ended. South Africa backed RENAMO and other rebels, whose attacks damaged railways and pipelines and kept the corridors unreliable. Lesotho, Swaziland and Botswana remained in a customs union with South Africa, and most members still traded heavily with it and sent migrant workers to its mines. SADCC itself depended on foreign donors, so one dependence was partly replaced by another.

Overall SADCC achieved a limited reduction in dependence, mainly in transport, but South Africa's economic power and its destabilisation meant that real economic liberation came only after apartheid ended.

hints: In (b), judge SADCC against its own original aims.
